items.title: Section: Leading a Community Rightly — Material Support Given Without Hidden Motive

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，性好攝受諸有情類，如法御眾，方便饒益。以無染心先與依止，以憐愍心現作饒益，然後給施如法衣服、飲食、臥具、病緣醫藥資身什物。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, by nature delighting in embracing beings, rightly lead their community according to the teaching, benefiting them through skilful means. ... With a mind entirely free of any hidden motive, they first provide support, acting for genuine benefit out of real compassion, and only then give lawfully obtained clothing, food, bedding, medicine, and other necessities.

items.zh: 若自無有，應從淨信長者、居士、婆羅門等求索與之。於己以法所獲如法衣服、飲食、諸坐臥具、病緣醫藥資身什物，與眾同用，自無隱費。
items.en: If one has nothing oneself, one should seek it from a faithful patron of means. Whatever is lawfully obtained in this way — clothing, food, bedding, medicine, and other necessities — is shared equally with the whole community; none of it is quietly kept back for private use.

items.title: Section: Teaching-Based Support — Cultivating the Buddha's Own Powers

items.zh: 於時時間，以其隨順八種教授而正教授，五種教誡而正教誡。此中所說教授、教誡，當知如前力種性品已廣分別。
items.en: At every fitting opportunity, one rightly instructs through the eight kinds of instruction, and rightly admonishes through the five kinds of admonishment. This instruction and admonishment should be understood exactly as already explained at length in the chapter on the lineage of the powers.

items.title: Section: Going Along With a Follower's Own Nature — Knowing Their Disposition, Then Practising Alongside Them

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於有情心性好隨轉。隨心轉時，先知有情若體若性。知體性已，隨諸有情所應共住，即應如是與其共住；隨諸有情所應同行，即應如是與彼同行。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, in their disposition, delight in going along with beings' own hearts. In going along, they first come to know a being's own underlying nature and character. Having known it, they dwell together in whatever way genuinely fits that being, and practice together in whatever way genuinely fits them.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩欲隨所化有情心轉，當審觀察，若於如是如是相事現行身語生他憂苦，如是憂苦若不令其出不善處安立善處，菩薩爾時於如是事現行身語，護彼心故，方便思擇勵力遮止令不現行。

items.title: Section: Weighing Whether Correction Genuinely Helps — And a Striking Exception When Compassion Requires Breaking the Rule

items.zh: 如是憂苦若能令其出不善處安立善處，菩薩爾時於如是事現行身語，住哀愍心，不隨如是有情心轉，方便思擇勵力策發要令現行。
items.en: If such distress is genuinely able to draw the offender out of an unwholesome state and settle them in a wholesome one, the bodhisattva does carry out the correction — abiding in a mind of genuine pity, not swayed by the offender's own reaction, deliberately and resolutely bringing the correction about.

items.zh: 若於如是他有情事現行身語令餘有情發生憂苦，如是憂苦若不令他、或餘有情、或不令二出不善處安立善處，菩薩爾時於如是事現行身語，護餘心故，方便思擇勵力遮止令不現行。如是憂苦若能令他、或餘有情、或能令二出不善處安立善處，菩薩爾時於如是事現行身語，住哀愍心，不隨如是有情心轉，方便思擇勵力策發要令現行。復審觀察，若於如是菩薩自事現行身語生他憂苦，如是現行身語二業非諸菩薩學處所攝，不順福德、智慧資糧，如是憂苦不能令他出不善處安立善處，菩薩爾時於如是事現行身語，護他心故，方便思擇勵力遮止令不現行。與此相違
items.en: Should carrying out that same correction cause distress to onlookers as well, ... the bodhisattva, in order to protect their minds, deliberately withholds it instead. ... Bodhisattvas, for the sake of benefiting others, may in specific circumstances even engage in a small portion of what would ordinarily be a genuinely wrong act — through this very cause, they do not violate the bodhisattva precepts at all, and generate great merit instead.

items.title: The Same Careful Weighing Applies to Bringing Joy, Not Just Sorrow

items.zh: 如生憂苦，如是廣說生於喜樂，隨其所應，當知亦爾。
items.en: Exactly as explained regarding causing distress, so too, in full detail, regarding bringing about joy — it should be understood as governed by the very same considerations.

items.title: Section: Going Along With Every Being — Never Provoking Anger, Always Reciprocating Celebration

items.zh: 又隨他心而轉菩薩，知他有情忿纏所纏，現前忿纏難可捨離，尚不讚歎，何況毀呰，即於爾時亦不諫誨。
items.en: Bodhisattvas going along with beings, knowing that someone is presently gripped by anger not easily released in the moment, do not even offer praise, let alone criticism; nor, at that same moment, do they attempt to counsel or correct them.

items.zh: 又隨他心而轉菩薩，他雖不來談論慶慰，尚應自往談論慶慰，何況彼來而不酬報。
items.en: Bodhisattvas going along with beings, even when another does not initiate conversation or celebration, should still initiate it themselves — how much more so, then, reciprocating when the other person does come to them.

items.title: Section: Never Deliberately Provoking Distress, Never Humiliating Another, Never Growing Prideful

items.zh: 又隨他心而轉菩薩，終不故意惱觸於他，唯除訶責諸犯過者，起慈悲心，諸根寂靜，如應訶責令其調伏。
items.en: Bodhisattvas going along with beings never deliberately provoke distress in another, except when reproaching someone who has genuinely erred — and even then, giving rise to compassion, the senses remaining calm, reproaching only as fitting, so as to help them settle their own conduct.

items.zh: 又隨他心而轉菩薩，終不嗤誚輕弄於他，令其𧹞愧不安隱住，亦不令其心生憂悔。雖能摧伏得勝於彼，而不彰其墮在負處。彼雖淨信，生於謙下，終不現相而起自高。
items.en: Bodhisattvas going along with beings never mock or belittle another, causing them shame or lingering regret. Even having genuinely bested another in debate, they never make a show of that person's defeat. And even when another, out of genuine faith, treats them with great humility, they never let that go to their head.

items.title: Section: Appropriate Closeness, Careful Speech, and Honouring Commitments With Grace

items.zh: 又隨他心而轉菩薩，於諸有情非不親近，不極親近，亦不非時而相親近。
items.en: Bodhisattvas going along with beings are never aloof, never excessively clingy, and never draw close to anyone at an unfitting moment.

items.zh: 又隨他心而轉菩薩，終不現前毀他所愛，亦不現前讚他非愛；非情交者不吐實誠，不屢希望，知量而受；若先許應他飲食等，終無假託不赴先祈，為性謙冲如法曉諭。
items.en: Bodhisattvas going along with beings never criticise, in front of someone, what that person loves, nor praise, in front of them, what they resent; with those whose friendship is not sincere, they do not reveal their true thoughts, do not make repeated requests, and accept what is offered only in fitting measure. Having once promised to share a meal or similar occasion, they never quietly excuse themselves from it under some pretext, always explaining themselves humbly and honestly if genuinely unable to attend.

blocks.text: How a bodhisattva leads others and lives harmoniously with them. The advice on tact is detailed and humane.

"With a mind free of hidden motive", one first provides for followers (Venerable Miào Jìng: first a place to stay). "If one has nothing, one seeks it from a faithful patron", and shares equally. Then one instructs and admonishes.

"They first come to know a being's underlying nature and character", then "dwell and practise alongside them". Master Cháng Bǎi: greed-dominant, anger-dominant, and so on, each needs a different approach.

"If causing distress can draw the offender out of an unwholesome state, the bodhisattva does it, with compassion." But "should the same correction cause distress to onlookers", one may hold back to protect their minds. The same weighing applies to bringing joy.
"Knowing someone is gripped by anger not easily released, they do not even offer praise, let alone criticism." They greet others first, "and reciprocate celebration".
They never cause distress "except when reproaching someone who has erred". "They never mock or belittle another." Having bested someone, they never display it.
"Never aloof, never excessively clingy, never drawing close at an unfitting moment." "They never criticise, in front of someone, what that person loves, nor praise what they resent."

quiz.q: In leading a community, "with a mind free of hidden motive, they first provide support." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "first provide support," and what does Master Cháng Bǎi stress?
options: Miào Jìng: first give them a place to live; Cháng Bǎi: not taking someone in so they will work for oneself
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "first provide support" means first giving them a place to stay. Master Cháng Bǎi: one does not take people in so they will work for oneself. Miào Jìng adds that the defiled motive would be wanting them as servants — cheap labour.

quiz.q: In leading a community through the teaching, with what does the treatise say one instructs and admonishes?
options: eight kinds of instruction and five kinds of admonishment, as explained in the chapter on the lineage of powers
quiz.why: "One rightly instructs through the eight kinds of instruction, and rightly admonishes through the five kinds of admonishment … as already explained at length in the chapter on the lineage of the powers." Master Cháng Bǎi: beings with much greed cultivate the object of impurity; those with much anger, loving-kindness.

quiz.q: In going along with beings' hearts, what does the treatise say bodhisattvas first come to know?
options: the being's underlying nature and character; then they dwell and practice together as fits
quiz.why: "In going along, they first come to know a being's own underlying nature and character. Having known it, they dwell together in whatever way genuinely fits." Venerable Miào Jìng: studying the dharma together and receiving offerings together is "dwelling together."

quiz.q: If correction can bring the offender to a wholesome state, the bodhisattva "abides in pity, not swayed by the offender's reaction." How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe the means here?
quiz.why: "If such distress is genuinely able to draw the offender out of an unwholesome state … the bodhisattva does carry out the correction — abiding in a mind of genuine pity." Venerable Miào Jìng: that is, taking compassion as the means.

quiz.q: Knowing someone is gripped by anger not easily released, what does the bodhisattva who goes along with beings do?
options: do not even praise, let alone criticise; nor counsel them at that moment
quiz.why: "Knowing that someone is presently gripped by anger not easily released, [they] do not even offer praise, let alone criticism; nor, at that same moment, do they attempt to counsel." Master Cháng Bǎi: it's like a great wall — speaking only hits the wall; wait until the anger passes.

quiz.q: The English renders this as "even having bested another in debate." How do the lectures read the line?
options: the bodhisattva should lose on purpose
the treatise only says "having prevailed," not "in debate"; Cháng Bǎi: let them save face; Miào Jìng: ordinary people, having won, always humiliate the loser
quiz.why: The treatise does not say "in debate"; the translator added it. Master Cháng Bǎi: it lets the other person save face. Venerable Miào Jìng: ordinary people, once they've beaten someone, always have to humiliate them a bit.

quiz.q: What is the measure of closeness for the bodhisattva who goes along with beings?
options: never aloof, never excessively close, and never at an unfitting time
quiz.why: "Never aloof, never excessively clingy, and never draw close to anyone at an unfitting moment." Master Cháng Bǎi: joining banquets, meals, and afternoon tea, rejoicing in others' happy occasions, is "not being aloof."
